text:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing ~2.3x p99 latency tail on MoE inference in prod for a small traffic slice. Traces point to an all-to-all hotspot during routing groups (8-GPU shards).

alex: Quick profile dump from the 03:12 window: 
```
p99 latency: 80ms -> 190ms
KV cache hit-rate: 84% (no big regress)
AllToAll (nv): 72.1ms (blocked, long wait)
NCCL allreduce: 12.3ms
Compute (matmuls + softmax): 48.6ms
Thread stalls: queue loop waiting on remote tokens
```

nina: Link to the trace? can we see per-expert fanout distribution? :mag:

alex: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/1965432100 (internal) — look at GPU 3/6 timeline, you can see repeated small alltoall calls with >2000 us gaps.

juan: What's the tensor/pipeline config for that deployment? did we change TP or DP recently? small routing imbalances can blow up if TP splits tokens weirdly.

alex: It's TP=2, PP=1, DP=4. No config change in prod, but we rolled a runtime kernel push yesterday that changed kernel selection heuristics for >512 seqs.

sasha: I pulled the sampled token-level routes from the trace. Fanout skew looks like: 
```
expert fanout histogram (sampled 10k tokens):
  fanout=1: 1,023
  fanout=2: 10,987
  fanout=3: 345,678
  fanout>=4: 1,200 (but long tails)
max tokens to same expert in batch: 7123
median expert occupancy: 48
```
This suggests a hot expert scenario for some prompts.

nina: Could KV cache distribution be amplifying this? If many tokens route to the same expert and cache lookups serialize, you get both comm and KV contention. Any signs of lock contention?

alex: Kernel traces show spikes inside our KV lookup path for multi-shard lookups (we do a gather across TP shards). Those look synchronous.

juan: Two quick hypotheses: (1) new kernel selection fell back to a slower path for certain seq-len -> increased per-token compute, exposing comm wait; (2) batching heuristics produce a batch composition with high expert colocation, creating super-fanout A2A loads.

sasha: Agreed. We should try toggling kernel_selector to the old heuristic and repro on canary. Also try our chunked overlap strategy: issue smaller sub-alltoall chunks to better overlap comm/compute.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 0.17.3 -> eng-runtime-canary started at 1965432200 by alex. :rocket:

nina: I'm going to run a targeted profiling job to capture per-expert busy times and NVLink utilization. Running: `bazel run //eng-runtime/prof:all2all_probe -- --group=8 --trace=1965432100`

juan: I'll reproduce locally with synthetic hot prompts (script in eng-runtime/tools/hot-expert-repro). Also test kernel toggle: `RUNTIME_KERNEL=legacy bazel run ...`

alex: Action items:
- nina: collect per-GPU NVLink p2p & nccl traces (+ flamegraphs) — due in 2h
- juan: local repro + kernel toggle, post perf diff — due EOD
- sasha: prepare canary rollback plan if 0.17.3 correlates — ping infra on fallback route config

sasha: One more note: batching heuristics currently group by sequence length -> if a batch happens to contain many tokens that route to same expert, our current prefix-preserving batching increases the probability of hotspot. Might need to inject a routing-aware jitter/balancer.

alex: Good call. If we can cheaply insert a pre-shuffle that spreads candidate tokens across experts (without harming cache hits too much) we might flatten the tail. Add to experiment list.

ops-bot: perf-alert: p99 > threshold for slice redwood-prod/moe-group-8 at 1965432250 — autoscale didn't trigger because this was within reserved capacity.

nina: Uploading NVLink / NCCL timeline and flamegraph: https://perf.internal/redwood/artifacts/1965432100/nvlink-ngc-flame.svg

juan: Early finding: legacy kernel path reduces alltoall latency by ~30% in repro, but increases compute time by ~5% (more efficient pack/unpack in new kernel but slower path in some branch). Looks like the kernel heuristic missed the hot path case.

alex: That's consistent with telemetry. Plan: short-term rollback of kernel selector heuristic on canary, run synthetic hot-expert tests, then evaluate routing-aware batching in mid-term. If kernel rollback fixes tail, we'll ship rollback and schedule batching change.

sasha: I'll draft a simple pre-shuffle patch (opt-in flag) that splits batches into N shards by hash(token-prefix) before routing. Should be quick to A/B.

alex: Thanks team. Please paste any short flamegraphs/snippets here. If anyone finds KV lookup serialization root cause, call it out immediately. :thumbsup:
